title: Market Propulsion: Gap-Scouting Framework for Emerging Model Niches
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, repeatable framework to identify high-leverage gaps in the open and hosted model landscape that could materially affect Redwood Inference’s product positioning (latency/cost/enterprise fit). The output will be a ranked signal catalogue and a short runbook for triggers that should create follow-up PM/Eng research tickets (capacity, quantization tests, legal review). Scope: competitive models (open checkpoints + hosted variants), quantization/compatibility signals, hardware affinity risk, enterprise fit (compliance, tokenizer/data provenance), and fallback economics (cost/latency delta to Redwood baseline). Deliverables: 1) Signal catalogue CSV (scored), 2) Scoring rubric doc in Confluence, 3) 5 prioritized hypothesis cards that map to concrete experiments (benchmarks or procurement probes), 4) Dashboard wireframe for periodic monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Signal catalogue exported as CSV with at least 25 candidate model variants and 10 signal columns (e.g., token_latency_ms, cost_per_1k, quant_compatibility, enterprise_license_risk)
Scoring rubric published to Confluence with weight rationale and reviewer sign-off from Research and Eng
Top 5 hypotheses have associated owners, experiment proposal (benchmark config), and estimated cost/effort
Runbook includes trigger thresholds for auto-creating follow-up Linear tickets (example triggers: cost delta > 2x, latency delta > 50ms, license change flagged)
Prototype dashboard mock uploaded to Drive and linked in the Confluence doc
tasks: Kickoff: align stakeholders and success metrics (PM/Research/Infra) - Asha
Define candidate model universe and sources (Hugging Face, community mirrors, vendor release notes) - Research
Design signal schema and normalized scoring ranges - PM + Research
Run quick probes on 10 sample models for latency and token cost at 512/2048 tokens - Eng
Populate catalogue and run scoring, generate ranked list

Create follow-up Linear tickets for top 3 hypotheses with benchmark specs
